subject: Strategic pricing pathway and commit-shift proposal for BlueHorizon renewal
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Gray <samuel.gray@bluehorizonlogistics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strategic pricing pathway and commit-shift proposal for BlueHorizon renewal

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a concise set of options on the table for BlueHorizon’s upcoming renewal so you can review with your finance and procurement teams. High level: we can combine a shorter-term price-hold with a staged commit increase and a one-time credit to smooth your unit economics while you complete traffic redistribution.

Attached is a clean proposal (bluehorizon_proposal_v3.pdf) with the two primary paths:
- Option A: 12-month renewal, 20% price-hold on current rates for the first 6 months, followed by a staged commit uplift (25% increase in reserved capacity) with an agreed credit of 15% applied against first-quarter usage.
- Option B: 24-month renewal, 10% price-hold for 12 months, smaller commit uplift (15%), and a blended credit structure (10% initial credit + 5% usage-based rebate after quarter 2).

Our priority is predictable costs for you while keeping performance SLAs in place. If procurement needs a firm amendment for internal review, I can draft a short amendment (one page) that captures the price-hold and credit terms and route it to legal. I’ve copied Aditya to lead the commercial paperwork and Monica to coordinate capacity/ops details.

Quick asks: could you confirm which option your CFO prefers (A or B) and whether they need an explicit price-hold end-date in the amendment text? If helpful, Aditya can schedule a 30-minute session with your finance team next week.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: bluehorizon_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal, 6 pages)
From: Samuel Gray <samuel.gray@bluehorizonlogistics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluehorizonlogistics.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategic pricing pathway and commit-shift proposal for BlueHorizon renewal

Laura —

Appreciate the options and the clear framing. A few quick notes from our side after an initial run by finance/procurement:
1) The CFO likes Option A for the shorter-term flexibility, but procurement asked whether we can move the effective price-hold to 9 months instead of 6. That gives us more runway while we migrate load to the new fleet.
2) The commit uplift is fine, but procurement asked if the 15% one-time credit can be structured as an upfront credit applied to the first invoice rather than a retrospective rebate. They want it visible in the first month P&L.
3) We will need a clear definition of what triggers the staged commit change (e.g., start date vs. usage threshold).

Can you and Aditya confirm these points and share a draft amendment that shows the price-hold ending after 9 months and the credit as an invoice-level line item? I’ll route to legal once we have text.

Thanks —
Sam
Samuel Gray
Head of Cloud Ops, BlueHorizon Logistics
samuel.gray@bluehorizonlogistics.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Gray <samuel.gray@bluehorizonlogistics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategic pricing pathway and commit-shift proposal for BlueHorizon renewal

Thanks, Sam — that’s helpful. Confirming we can update Option A as follows:
- Price-hold extended to 9 months (explicit end date: 2028-04-01).
- One-time credit converted to an upfront invoice credit line (15% of projected Q1 usage based on the attached proposal numbers); credit will reduce first invoice balance.
- Staged commit uplift will be triggered by an agreed start date (2028-04-01) rather than usage thresholds to keep rollout predictable; we can include an option for automated trigger if usage remains >= 90% of baseline for 2 consecutive weeks.

Aditya — can you please prepare a short amendment that captures those three points (price-hold end date, invoice credit mechanism, start-date trigger) and include the numerical credit calculation so procurement can see the P&L impact? Monica, can you confirm runway for the requested capacity uplift and whether any rollout penalties need to be called out?

Rishi — I’ve looped you for awareness; if finance wants to approve the invoice-credit mechanism we’ll need a short note on revenue recognition/timing.

If everyone is aligned, I’ll upload amendment_BH-4521_draft.docx and a one-page summary to the HubSpot deal record and route the DocuSign link.

Laura
